newsitem.title: FINLAND: OKOBANK SEES IN POSITION FOR 1997 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: OKOBANK SEES IN POSITION FOR 1997 PROFIT.

text.p: Finnish OKOBANK said on Tuesday in a statement it expected to be in a good position to post a profit in 1997.

"OKOBANK Consolidated will be in a good position to achieve a profitable result in the current year, too," OKO said after reporting a 230 million markka operating profit after credit losses in 1996, up from a 47 million markka loss the previous year.
"OKOBANK Consolidated's result improved markedly in 1996," the bank said.

"The improved result was due to significant growth in commission and fee income and in net income from securities trading," it said, adding credit losses had also fallen. Credit losses fell 55 percent to 171 million markka.
Non-performing claims fell by 51 percent to 295 million markka at end-1996 and zero-interest claims fell to 108 million markka from slightly over 500 million a year earlier.
Staff and administrative costs fell and OKOBANK's income-to-expenses ratio rose to 1.43 from 1.33.
